steps.name: Load, QC, and log2-transform TPM matrix
caveats: This is a TPM table with no raw counts or quantification directories — do not attempt to reconstruct counts or apply count-based normalization/dispersion models
12000 gene rows and 12 samples is small; do not over-provision memory
steps.question: Given the 12000-gene x 12-sample TPM table (tpm.csv) and the 6 lesional vs 6 control metadata.csv, what does the sample-level structure (PCA/hierarchical clustering, library-size proxy via total TPM, missingness) look like before testing for differential expression, and are there any outlier samples or mismatches between the TPM columns and the metadata condition labels?
acceptance_criteria: All 12 samples in tpm.csv are matched 1:1 to metadata.csv condition labels (6 lesional, 6 control) with no unmatched columns
A log2(TPM+1) matrix is produced and saved for downstream steps
Low-expression genes (e.g., TPM below a stated threshold in fewer than the smaller group size of samples) are flagged/filtered with the filter rule and resulting gene count reported explicitly
PCA and/or hierarchical clustering plot is generated showing condition separation or lack thereof, and any outlier sample is explicitly called out rather than silently dropped

steps.name: Differential expression: lesional vs control via limma-trend on log2(TPM)
caveats: Do not use voom() — it is designed for count data and library-size-derived precision weights, neither of which exist here

State explicitly in the output that this is a limma-trend analysis on TPM-derived log2 values because raw counts were unavailable, which is a documented but less standard approach than a full count-based DE pipeline
With n=6 per group the power to detect modest effect sizes is limited; report this alongside the DE gene count
steps.question: Using the filtered log2(TPM+1) matrix from T1S1, which genes are significantly differentially expressed between the 6 psoriasis lesional and 6 control skin samples (unpaired, single-batch design), and what are their effect sizes (log2 fold-change) and significance (moderated t-statistic, BH-adjusted p-value)?
acceptance_criteria: A limma linear model (design ~ condition) is fit on log2(TPM+1) values with eBayes(trend=TRUE) — the correct approach for pre-normalized continuous expression data without raw counts, not voom (which requires counts) and not DESeq2/edgeR (which require counts)
Full results table (gene, logFC, AveExpr, t, P.Value, adj.P.Val) is produced for all filtered genes, sorted by adjusted p-value

Number of genes at adj.P.Val < 0.05 (and a stated |logFC| threshold, e.g. 1) is reported explicitly, with the caveat that TPM-derived limma-trend p-values may be conservative or liberal relative to a full count-based pipeline noted in the output
A volcano plot of logFC vs -log10(adj.P.Val) is generated highlighting top significant genes

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes (WikiPathways, Reactome, MSigDB hallmark/canonical)
caveats: Reactome GMT covers all species in one file — must be filtered to Homo sapiens using ReactomePathways.txt (join on stable ID) before use
WikiPathways/MSigDB set names need parsing per each file's documented delimiter convention before use
steps.question: Which biological pathways and processes are over-represented among the genes differentially expressed between psoriasis lesional and control skin (from T1S2), using human WikiPathways, Reactome, MSigDB hallmark, and MSigDB canonical (BioCarta/KEGG MEDICUS/PID) gene sets?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis (or fgsea preranked on the full moderated-t statistic) is run separately against the human WikiPathways GMT, the Reactome GMT (filtered to Homo sapiens via ReactomePathways.txt), the MSigDB hallmark GMT, and the MSigDB canonical (BioCarta/KEGG MEDICUS/PID) GMTs
Results include gene set name, overlap/leading-edge genes, enrichment score/odds ratio, and BH-adjusted p-value for each reference collection

Findings are cross-checked for consistency with the well-established psoriasis biology (IL-17/keratinocyte differentiation/innate immune signatures) and any departure from that expectation is flagged rather than silently reported
If any of the four reference sets is missing at run time, the step reports which ran and which were skipped rather than failing outright

steps.name: STRING PPI network context for top DE genes
caveats: protein.links file is space-delimited despite .txt extension and ~83MB gzipped with ~13.7M rows (undirected, double-counted edges) — load efficiently and do not treat the full low-confidence graph as meaningful for distance measures
Restrict work to the gene list from T1S2, do not attempt full-graph analysis
steps.question: Do the top differentially expressed genes between lesional and control skin (from T1S2) form a more highly connected subnetwork than expected by chance in the human STRING protein-protein interaction network, and which hub genes emerge?
acceptance_criteria: STRING protein.links (joined to protein.info for gene symbols) is subset to edges with combined_score >= 700 (high-confidence cut) before any network construction, per the reference file's documented convention

The top DE gene set (e.g., adj.P.Val < 0.05) is mapped onto STRING gene symbols and the induced subnetwork's edge count and degree distribution are reported, with hub genes (highest degree) named explicitly
Report explicitly that STRING is a generic functional-association network, not a psoriasis-specific one, so any 'hub' claim is descriptive/topological, not a proven psoriasis mechanism

steps.name: Immune/keratinocyte program signature scoring (ssGSEA) on log2(TPM)
caveats: GSVA/ssGSEA on TPM-derived values (rather than counts) is standard practice and appropriate here
n=6 per group limits power for per-signature statistical testing; treat results as exploratory
steps.question: Using the log2(TPM+1) matrix (T1S1) and MSigDB hallmark gene sets, do lesional psoriasis samples show higher single-sample enrichment scores for inflammatory/immune hallmark programs (e.g., inflammatory response, IL6/JAK/STAT3, TNFA signaling, interferon response) and keratinocyte/epithelial-relevant programs compared to control, and is the difference significant across the 6 vs 6 samples?
acceptance_criteria: GSVA or ssGSEA scores are computed per sample against the MSigDB hallmark gene sets on the log2(TPM+1) matrix
Per-hallmark-set lesional-vs-control comparison (e.g., Wilcoxon or moderated t-test on the score matrix) with BH-adjusted p-values is reported

Explicitly state this is a descriptive bulk-tissue signature score, not a cell-type deconvolution, since no validated LM22/xCell signature-matrix reference was found in the environment for this run — if one is confirmed present at execution time, immune cell-type deconvolution (e.g., MCPcounter, quantiseqr, or ConsensusTME, all installed) may be added as a supplementary read, otherwise this caveat must appear in the output

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE from TPM-only skin RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples: 6 lesional, 6 control skin, unpaired, single batch) with no raw counts and no quantification directories — count-based tools (DESeq2, edgeR exact/GLM, standard voom-from-counts) cannot be used because they require integer counts to model the mean-variance relationship via a negative binomial or count-based precision weight. The only valid path on TPM-only input is to log2-transform the TPM values and apply limma's moderated t-test with the empirical Bayes 'trend' option (eBayes(..., trend=TRUE)), which was designed for exactly this situation — continuous, already-normalized expression values rather than raw counts (as documented in the limma/Bioconductor RNA-seq workflow literature, e.g. Law et al. 2016, and the 'why weight' extension by Liu et al. 2015 for count-based data, which does not apply here since no counts exist). Track 1 does data preparation and the core DE test. Track 2 takes the resulting gene list/ranked statistic into pathway and pathway-activity context using WikiPathways, Reactome, MSigDB hallmark and canonical (BioCarta/KEGG MEDICUS/PID) human gene sets, all confirmed present for Homo sapiens in the reference store. Track 3 adds an STRING PPI-network view of the top DE genes for connectivity context, and a skin-relevant immune/cell-composition read (via ssGSEA/GSVA over available cell signatures, since no LM22/xCell signature matrix reference is present in the store) to flag whether shifts look driven by immune infiltration versus keratinocyte-intrinsic programs — reported as descriptive, not causal. No survival/PK/safety/compound data is present, so no translational-safety, pkpd, or cheminformatics steps are included.
